newsitem.title: THAILAND: Bank of Thailand midrate lowest since Sept 1989.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Thailand midrate lowest since Sept 1989.

text.p: The Bank of Thailand's dollar/baht midrate slipped on Wednesday to 26.08 baht to the dollar, the lowest since September 1989, from 26.06 on Tuesday.
Central bank spokeswoman Duangmanee Vongprathip told Reuters the baht weakness was caused by the strengthening of the dollar and was not due to Thai fundamentals.
"It is all external factors, and has nothing to do with our economic fundamentals which remain strong," she said.
Duangmanee said the central bank will monitor the money market closely and may keep interbank rate high if necessary to curb dollar/baht speculation.

"The Bank of Thailand will see to it that excess liquidity will not be used for currency speculation. But at the same time, we will make sure that what we do will not affect business either," she said.
